clue.text: Marsupial, possibly remaining as at start of today?

indicators.note: 'possibly' suggests one of several arrangements, so the preceding words are to be rearranged

parts.note: three words taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of today

explanation.surface: A wistful question about whether some rare marsupial still survives as of this morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Marsupial' is fair: the thylacine, or Tasmanian tiger, is thought extinct, which is why 'remaining as at today' is a poignant surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian tiger, or thylacine, was a striped carnivorous pouched mammal of Tasmania, so it is an example of a marsupial.

clue.text: Excellent tippler, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: tops means the very best
a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, someone decides a drinker is first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a first-class tippler is a heavy drinker. Both words are read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a drunkard, someone who tosses back pots of ale.

clue.text: Minimal salary: sadly we get basics, us, receiving almost the limit

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the shortened word goes inside the others
sadly means badly here, so the words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost all of something stops just short, so its final letter goes

parts.note: the end is the furthest limit

explanation.surface: Workers complain that their meagre pay covers only basics for the likes of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word joins the other letters before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsistence wage is pay barely enough to keep someone alive, the lowest income that sustains life.

clue.text: Offering praise aloud, try getting excited following artist's debut

indicators.note: following places the rearranged letters after the single letter
a debut is a first appearance, so just the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of artist

indicators.note: excited particles move about wildly, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cheers loudly, urging an artist making a first appearance to have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aloud' looks like a sound signal, but its letters are simply part of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory means expressing excessive admiration or flattery, so it describes something offering praise.

clue.text: Not wise to collar old woman regarding choice of expression

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A warning that it would be foolish to nab some elderly lady over the words she chose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is slang for one's mother or wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic describes language natural to native speakers, so it concerns the choice of phrasing.

clue.text: Requirements observed to rise after daughter takes up residence

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading from bottom to top, so letters run backwards
taking up residence means moving in, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: seen means observed
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: House rules noted as going up once a daughter moves in.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal happens first, then the single letter is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things that are necessary, the same as requirements.

clue.text: Raging that is seen around desert

indicators.note: one thing seen around another surrounds it, so it goes on either side

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: A fierce storm or fury spotted around some barren desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy place, but it is the verb: to rat on is to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means extremely angry, so it matches raging as a synonym.

clue.text: Aromatherapy source still popular with doctor, having edge on treatment of sore

indicators.note: a treatment works on something and changes it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: even, as in even more, means still
in means fashionable
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a rim is an edge
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A natural oil remains popular with doctors for treating a sore.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is the British general practitioner, the doctor you see first.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening primrose is a plant whose seed oil is widely sold for complementary therapies, making it an aromatherapy ingredient.

clue.text: Doubtful character, notwithstanding that large amount of service in church

indicators.note: a large amount is most but not the whole, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: tho' is a short form of though
the Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A sceptic who nonetheless attends a great deal of church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubtful character' refers to Doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection without seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas doubted Christ's rising until he saw the wounds, so he is the Bible's doubter.

clue.text: Subject, universal form of gambling, not able to be discussed

parts.note: a standard abbreviation of subject, as in grammar
U is the film classification for universal
dice is a game of chance played for stakes

explanation.surface: A topic involving a universal kind of gambling that is somehow off limits for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: U for universal is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub judice is Latin for 'under a judge': a matter before the courts that may not be publicly commented on.

clue.text: Foremost character, first in expedition, probing mountain height

indicators.note: something probing pushes inside another thing, so one piece goes into the next

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: 'first in' a word picks out only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of expedition
h is the standard abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: The leading figure of an expedition explores the height of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foremost character' sounds like a leader of the party, but a character here is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so it is literally the foremost written character.

clue.text: Foremost in performance, tidy bit of acting

parts.note: prim means neat and proper

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its leading letter

parts.note: the first letter of acting

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict on a show: the best part was a neat little piece of acting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a phrase: prima, as in prima donna or prima ballerina, names the leading performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima is Italian for first, used for the principal singer or dancer in a company's performances.

clue.text: A lot of quality in military canteen — Frenchman's unusual influence

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the mess is where service personnel eat

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: merit is worth or excellence
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in the army mess exerts some strange pull thanks to his many fine qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Frenchman stands for 'has', linking wordplay to definition. Mesmerism is named after Franz Mesmer and his 'animal magnetism'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesmerism is hypnotic control over another person, a strange and compelling power over their mind.

clue.text: Retaliation — keep after it, blocking pretentious stuff

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so these letters go within the next ones

parts.note: tat is showy, tasteless goods

indicators.note: 'after' places the first named item behind the second in reading order

parts.note: taken as written
a keep is the stronghold of a castle

explanation.surface: Revenge advice: keep after it and obstruct all that pretentious rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb meaning continue, but it is the noun for a castle's tower. Tat is British slang for cheap, gaudy objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is an idiom for paying back an injury in kind, matching each blow with one of your own.

clue.text: Camera accessory starts to take every top-hole shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so these letters are knocked out of order
the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of take and every
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on getting first-rate photos: begin with a good lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a photograph, fitting the camera theme, but it is the signal to rearrange. Top-hole is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens magnifies distant subjects, an attachment for a camera.

clue.text: Identify America? But this is a European river

parts.note: to tag something is to label or mark it
the United States

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to point out America, then is told this is actually a river in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sets up America only to undercut it: the answer is a river in Iberia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian peninsula, flowing through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.

clue.text: Run out of English money? Observe where you'd get dollars

indicators.note: out of here means missing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: tenners are ten-pound notes
r is the cricket abbreviation for run, the letter removed
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: Someone abroad has run out of pounds and is told where to find dollars instead.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note. The definition is vague on purpose: any US state uses dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is a state of the USA, whose currency is the dollar, so it is a place you'd be paid in dollars.

clue.text: Cheerful, small and comical, showing no trace of fear

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: having no trace of something means that thing is removed entirely

parts.note: comical means funny
F is fear's initial, the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Describing a fearless, cheerful, funny little person.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter of fear is dropped, a common convention when 'trace' signals a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny disposition is a bright, happy one, so sunny is a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Source of oil's identical with large force departing

indicators.note: things departing leave, so those letters drop out

parts.note: selfsame means exactly the same
L is the abbreviation for large
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: An oil well that matches a big military force pulling out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', the link. 'Large force' looks like an army, but it gives two separate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed for an oil used widely in cooking, so the plant is an oil source.

clue.text: Scrawl and circle, marking dates in some way

indicators.note: a scrawl is messy writing, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking a diary: scribble and ring the important days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrawl' looks like part of the diary-marking scene, but it is the signal to rearrange the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendric means relating to a calendar, the system by which days and dates are recorded.

clue.text: Dispute — it's French, involving old religious books

indicators.note: involving means including, so the French phrase surrounds the books

parts.note: c'est is French for it is
o is the abbreviation for old
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An argument in France over some ancient scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old religious books' looks like OT, the Old Testament, but splits into O for old and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim is to challenge or argue against it, the same as to dispute it.

clue.text: Second squad's cool mode of transport

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a squad is a team, plus the possessive s
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: The reserve team's trendy way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on squad's supplies a letter rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a vessel driven by steam engines, a means of travelling by sea.

clue.text: Beset by mire, team's first half's quiet

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on every side, so the letters are enclosed

parts.note: mire is mud or bog

indicators.note: the first half of a word is its opening portion only

parts.note: the front half of the four letters of team

explanation.surface: Bogged down in a quagmire, the team was subdued during the first half of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 's, after half, stands for 'is' and links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted means softened or subdued in sound, so muted means much the same as quiet.

clue.text: Poet's a big hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ancient Greek author of the Iliad and the Odyssey
second meaning: in baseball, a home run

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a popular poet; the 's means 'is' and joins two unrelated meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the legendary Greek epic poet, and in baseball slang a homer is a home run struck clean out of the park.

clue.text: Novel mentality, to some extent wooden

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the phrase is used, here a run of letters within it

parts.note: the letters straddling the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: A critic calls a novel's outlook rather stiff and lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' wants its figurative sense of stiff, but here it literally means made of wood, specifically elm.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmen is an archaic adjective meaning made of elm timber, so it is a kind of wooden.

clue.text: Satisfied, having embraced one's intended

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the outer word wraps around another

parts.note: a need that is met is satisfied
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Someone is contented after hugging their fiancé or fiancée.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like the noun for a betrothed partner, but the answer is the past participle meaning planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past participle of mean, used to say something was planned or purposed.

clue.text: Gem displays bottom quality

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare backside
tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a voice

explanation.surface: A precious stone reveals that it is of the lowest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom quality' reads as poorest grade; split differently, mooning is baring one's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstone is a pearly feldspar cut and polished as a semi-precious stone for jewellery.

clue.text: Brutally destroyed revolt, seeing off Republican former President

indicators.note: something treated brutally is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
to see off is to get rid of, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A former President who crushed an uprising and got rid of a Republican rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt in reverse: Roosevelt was himself a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt was the 26th President of the United States, serving 1901 to 1909.
